pairs: Wisdom has built a house for herself.
Misit ancillas suas ut vocarent ad arcem et ad mœnia civitatis.
She has sent her maids to call out to the tower and to the fortified walls of the city,
Si quis est parvulus, veniat ad me.
“If anyone is little, let him come to me.”
And to the unwise, she has said:
et bibite vinum quod miscui vobis.
and drink the wine that I have mixed for you.
and walk by the ways of prudence.”
Qui erudit derisorem, ipse injuriam sibi facit,
Whoever teaches a mocker causes injury to himself.
et qui arguit impium, sibi maculam generat.
And whoever argues with the impious produces a blemish on himself.
Do not be willing to argue with a mocker,
Present an opportunity to the wise,
and wisdom shall be added to him.
and he will hurry to receive it.
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom,
and knowledge of holiness is prudence.
Per me enim multiplicabuntur dies tui,
your days will be multiplied and years of life will be added to you.
you will be so for yourself.
But if you would be one who ridicules,
you alone shall carry the evil.
plenaque illecebris, et nihil omnino sciens,

sat at the entrance of her house on a seat,
super sellam in excelso urbis loco,
in a high place of the city,

Qui est parvulus declinet ad me.

And he did not know that giants are there,
